finding.claim: The admin permission check in purge is called but its boolean result is discarded, so purge runs for any user regardless of permissions.
finding.source: Any user who can reach the purge route (handlers.go:24), via the user object from userFrom(r) at line 25

trace.note: u := userFrom(r) loads the caller's user
checkPerm(u, "admin") returns false for non-admins, but the result is ignored

finding.guards_checked: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) is the only check and its return value is unused, so it enforces nothing. The sibling rotateKeys (handlers.go:31-38) uses mustPerm with an early return and is SAFE, so purge is the inconsistent handler. No auth middleware or route table is in the repo, so route-level protection could not be verified.

verdict.guard_found: checkPerm (handlers.go:12-14) is the only permission check in purge, and its bool return is discarded as a bare statement at handlers.go:26, so it enforces nothing. The correct pattern is mustPerm with an early return, as in rotateKeys (handlers.go:33-34). No route-level auth middleware is in the repo to check.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches handlers.go:24-28: checkPerm at line 26 returns a bool that is discarded, so purgeAll() at line 27 runs for any caller that reaches the handler, while rotateKeys at lines 33-34 correctly returns early via mustPerm. The attacker is an authenticated low-privilege user, since the handler does not check admin. The one caveat is that route registration is not in the repo, so any route-level protection there could not be verified.
